title: With Stately Towers and Bulwarks Strong
description: With Stately Towers and Bulwarks Strong in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 655 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Jewish and the Christian Zion. Ps. 48”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: With state-ly towers and bul-warks strong, Un-ri-valled and a-lone, Loved theme of man-y a sacred song, God's ho-ly cit-y shone.

lines: With stately towers and bulwarks strong,
Loved theme of many a sacred song,
Thus fair was Zion's chosen seat,
Yet fairer, and in strength complete,
The faithful of each clime and age
Built on a rock, with idle rage
In vain may hostile bands alarm,
How weak, how powerless is each arm,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
